transcript.text: Hi everyone, before I finalize the package for Aria Vale's remote appearance in the festival's streamed closing program, I need to check with our broadcast engineer and rights manager. We've got a live 20-minute segment planned for the worldwide stream — are there any production requirements or clearance issues I should know about before I send the final specs to production?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, I need to flag a major production issue. My post-rehearsal network test showed that the venue cannot maintain reliable two-way latency for a live performance. However, it can reliably play an artist-approved file — but that file must be exactly 7 minutes or shorter, delivered as 1080p SDR with stereo audio. I completed this test after the last production meeting and haven't entered the result in the production log yet. This means the planned live 20-minute segment isn't feasible from a technical standpoint.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Maya, I have a clearance constraint I need to flag. My written distributor confirmation, which I received this morning while the clearance file was being updated, permits Aria Vale's appearance only in the United States and Canada. The stream must be geoblocked everywhere else. Additionally, the on-screen credit must read exactly 'Aria Vale — Closing Performance.' So the current plan for a worldwide stream conflicts with the territorial restriction, and the credit specification needs to be built into the package.
transcript.speaker: A3
